The firm’s inability to generate returns is further evidenced by a negative ROA of -6.23% and a negative ROE of -11.6%, both of which significantly underperform their respective sector benchmarks [E7, E8]. Despite these fundamental failures, the market is pricing the stock at a premium to the sector’s book value, suggesting that current expectations are disconnected from the company’s actual delivery [E6, E54].

The stock’s position at 6% of its 52-week range [E4] represents a significant entry point for investors who recognize that the current price-to-book ratio of 1.51x [E1] is actually more attractive than the sector benchmark of 1.76x [E6]. By focusing solely on short-term headwinds, the bear fails to account for the company's historical capacity for profit expansion [E18] and the potential for a rebound from current depressed valuation levels [E4].
